gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-old-persi: Noto Sans Old Persian lets its open counters breathe, with a lofty lowercase that stands tall. Groovy's single constant line width stays playful and loose beside it, so a longer passage would read clean and contemporary, with a grin up top.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdi: Friendly is Groovy's whole mood, with round letters and curves that carry no stress at all. And Noto Sans Old Sogdian, with its tall x-height and crisp wide mouths, gives it a sensible partner, while Groovy earns its keep big and brief.

gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Groovy brings a funky, loosely tracked lowercase with no thin strokes to vanish in glare. Noto Sans Oriya follows with generous gaps in its curves and small letters nearly as tall as its capitals, so you can let the sans body run modest in size.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-osage: Groovy draws everything with no thick-and-thin modulation, and its c nearly seals shut. Noto Sans Osage takes over with inflated bowls and sweeping open curves, so a longer passage in the plain sans would feel approachable and full.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Friendly and a bit funky, Groovy leans on closed shapes. Noto Sans Osmanya opens everything up, with easy s turns and a lowercase that towers over its capitals, and that closed-versus-open contrast is what makes the pairing click.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hm: Groovy's constant-width arms and legs, with a c that almost closes, are the first thing you notice. gen-dafont-groovy-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Groovy draws its letters like a ballpoint pen, loose and friendly. Noto Sans Palmyrene is the opposite number, with curves stopping short and compressed ascenders, and that gap between a looping display and a tight, clean text is the pair's best trick.
